answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by verifying nodes via acoustic ranging across a tidal lagoon. Nodes emit ultrasonic pulses timed by quartz oscillators, recording echoes scattered by roots of a shoreline vine. Forging identities forces an adversary to deploy dedicated physical transceivers across distinct coordinates, as localized acoustic scattering cannot be simulated digitally. However, storm turbulence degrades echo coherence, occasionally causing honest nodes to fail verification.
